name: Hang En cave expedition (Swallow Cave)
region: Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park, Quang Tri (formerly Quang Binh)
why: Down through jungle and river crossings to the Doong valley, then a night on a sand beach inside one of the largest caves in the world.
book: Only as a guided tour with Oxalis Adventure, the licensed operator: 2 days, ages 16-70, up to 16 guests, with guides, porters and a cook. Fitness test: a 5 km run in 45 minutes. Oxalis counts about 25 km of trekking plus 3 km of caving over the two days. Runs December to August; book months ahead.
water: The tour provides filtered, boiled water and all meals. Carry 2 litres for the trek out.
dangers: Many river crossings, knee-deep or more; flash floods after heavy rain close the trek.
Slippery rock, mud and leeches in the jungle; boulders and darkness inside the cave.
Heat and humidity from April to August, and a 450 m climb back up to the road on day 2.
turnaround: The guides decide: after heavy rain or with rising rivers the tour is postponed or turned back.

points.name: Trailhead on the Ho Chi Minh Road West
points.note: The tour van drops you on the jungle road above the Rao Thuong valley. The path drops steeply through forest to the stream.

points.name: Ban Doong village
points.note: A small Bru-Van Kieu village with stilt houses on the valley floor, cut off from roads. Lunch stop.

points.name: Hang En entrance and camp
points.note: The river runs into a huge mouth full of swallows. Camp on the sand beach by the underground lake; back the same way on day 2.
